summary: GDPR frontend fix (iter93bo) validated: in 'Nouvelle ACP' wizard create mode, no pre-emptive fetch/display of orphan owners. Recap shows '0 proprietaire(s) charge(s)' + 'Aucun - importez un PDF/CSV pour continuer'. Cross-checked with 56-68 orphan owners returned by /api/owners?include_unassigned=true — none of their email/name/aux_code appear anywhere in the HTML across all 5 substeps (PROPRIETAIRES, PROMOTEUR, LOTS, AFFECTATION, MUTATIONS). GDPR / Chinese-wall leak is fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: CoproprietesPage.js is 1874 lines — should be split into smaller modules (wizard, import, lots, owners) for maintainability.
DialogContent warnings in console: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby' — add DialogDescription for accessibility.
Edit-mode fetch (line 108) uses copropriete_id='all' + include_unassigned=true. Confirm backend filters by syndic_id server-side to avoid cross-syndic leakage in edit mode too.
seed_data_creation: None (used existing 56-68 orphan owners in DB as the leak canary).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test flow: login admin@copro.be, /coproprietes, click 'Nouvelle ACP', fill name -> Suivant, fill dates -> Suivant lands on '2. PROPRIETAIRES' substep. Verify no orphan owner PII in page HTML by cross-referencing /api/owners?include_unassigned=true&copropriete_id=all. Edit-mode 'Modifier' button was not automatically clickable in my script (likely inside a dropdown/menu); worth revisiting if edit-mode-specific behavior needs verification, but the create-mode fix (the reported bug) is confirmed.
rca of the issue: Original bug: useEffect on dialogOpen unconditionally fetched /owners?include_unassigned=true and setOwners(...), causing 11+ orphan owners' name+email+aux_code to render in the wizard step 2 BEFORE any user upload -> GDPR breach. Fix at CoproprietesPage.js:107-115 branches on `editing`: create mode -> setOwners(sessionOwners) only; edit mode -> preserved fetch. Verified: 0 rows displayed pre-upload, 'Aucun - importez PDF/CSV' message shown, zero PII leak on any of the 5 substeps.
